conventions.convention: Assume AC; positive finite state and noise dimensions; T>0; N≥1; h=T/N; Euclidean vector and Frobenius matrix norms. Coefficients are jointly Borel, globally Lipschitz in state, satisfy squared linear growth, and have a half-Hölder time modulus.
Brownian motion is adapted, and every future increment is independent of the current filtration. X₀ is measurable at time zero and square-integrable.
The recorded step process uses Yₖ on [tₖ,tₖ₊₁) and Y_N at T; stochastic integration uses Yₖ on (tₖ,tₖ₊₁]. The continuous interpolation agrees with the recursion at every endpoint.
The step-integral identity means equality at every time on one measurable probability-one event; it is called indistinguishability when the probability space is complete.
Uniform moment bounds require 0<h≤1 and a matching initial moment for each fixed finite p≥2. They bound sup_t E|Y_t|^p, without asserting E sup_t |Y_t|^p.

load_bearing.statement: Under the hypotheses of alg-euler-maruyama, 0<h≤1, and E|X₀|^p<∞ for fixed finite p≥2, the step process has a predictable representative and the interpolation is well-defined, adapted and continuous. The grid, step-process and interpolation pointwise p-moments are bounded by C(1+E|X₀|^p), uniformly in h; E|Y_t−bar Y_t|²≤Ch(1+E|X₀|²).
For its specified coefficient, Brownian and initial-value data, set Y₀=X₀ and, for k=0,…,N−1, form ΔWₖ=W_tₖ₊₁−W_tₖ and set Yₖ₊₁=Yₖ+b(tₖ,Yₖ)h+σ(tₖ,Yₖ)ΔWₖ.

For p≥2, 0≤δ≤1, an F_s-measurable U∈L^p, an independent N_m(0,δI_m) increment, and measurable coefficients satisfying squared linear growth, V=U+δb_s(U)+σ_s(U)(W_s₊δ−W_s) satisfies E(|V|^p|F_s)≤(1+Cδ)|U|^p+Cδ and E(|V−U|²|F_s)≤Cδ(1+|U|²), with constants independent of s,δ,U.

Assume AC and filtration-relative Brownian increment independence. On a finite partition, square-integrable F_tₖ-measurable coefficients define a square-integrable predictable step process. Every continuous integral version agrees on one measurable probability-one event, at every time, with the corresponding finite stopped-increment sum. Coefficients need not be bounded.

For the recursion of alg-euler-maruyama, define bar Y_t=Yₖ on [tₖ,tₖ₊₁), bar Y_T=Y_N, and Y_t=Yₖ+b(tₖ,Yₖ)(t−tₖ)+σ(tₖ,Yₖ)(W_t−W_tₖ) on [tₖ,tₖ₊₁]. Its integral representation uses predictable left-open, right-closed coefficient steps after square integrability is established.

published_dependencies.used_for: Declared ambient choice assumption inherited through Brownian, normal-law and Itô interfaces.
Vector Gaussian increment laws, scalar-coordinate interpretation and common-event path continuity; filtration-relative independence is separately assumed.
Independent standard-normal coordinate realization and centered covariance/second-moment formulas.
Predictable rectangle generators, deterministic predictable indicators and measurability of finite-step processes.
Bounded elementary coefficient convention and irrelevance of finitely many deterministic time values to product-measure classes.
Explicit finite stopped-Brownian-increment formula for bounded elementary integrands.
L² construction from elementary approximants, deterministic-time truncation and consistency with elementary integrals.
Existence and common-probability-one-event uniqueness of continuous integral versions.
Vanishing L² coefficient tails in the finite-step truncation argument.
Promotion of deterministic-time integral identities to simultaneous identities by continuity.
L² triangle inequality and separation of integral equivalence classes.
Gaussian density used to derive all finite absolute moments in the one-step estimate.
Bounding the iterated grid-moment recursion by exp(CT).

alerts.finding: The Facts & Assumptions block is duplicated after the Proof heading: the same Given paragraph and [F1]–[F12] entries appear again. For example, '[F9] For a continuous adapted process, the supremum on [0,t] equals the supremum over rational times in [0,t] together with t, and is F_t-measurable' occurs in both blocks. This is redundant presentation and repeats the fact labels.

The complete Given, [F1], [F2] and [A1]–[A3] block is repeated after the Proof heading. For example, '[A3] AC is included because [F1] carries that assumption from the Doob and Brownian Itô interfaces' appears in both blocks. This duplicates the assumptions and their labels.

seams_checked.note: Checked both interfaces. The scheme's moment argument does not import exact-solution existence or moments. The additive-noise example imports the strong-solution definition and explicitly supplies its complete usual filtration, adapted Brownian motion, initial value and simultaneous integral identity.

The strong-rate consumer retains 0<h≤1, the coefficient/time-modulus contract, initial L² data, endpoint conventions and pointwise Euler moments/increments. The weak-rate consumer retains matching initial L^p moments and adds explicit backward regularity. Neither citation attributes path-supremum moments or a convergence rate to the batch-2 moment theorem.
